findings.title: Stop gapped through at entry yields a zero-R 'stop' trade with a wrong-side initial_stop reported as positive risk
findings.failure_scenario: Decision at 09:40 (close 100), long with stop 99.0; the 09:41 bar opens at 98 (below the stop). Backtesting opens the trade at 98 and the SL (reprocessed on the entry bar) fills at min(open, stop)=98 in the same minute. The trade table records side=long, entry_price=98, exit_price=98, initial_stop=99 (above the entry), risk_per_share=1.0 (abs() hides the sign), pnl=-costs, r_multiple=0, exit_reason='stop', bars_held=0. The trade counts toward trade count / stop-rate / win-rate statistics although no risk was ever defined for it, and `initial_stop` is on the wrong side of the fill without any flag.
findings.evidence: Demonstrated with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dustin-Projects-strategy/bd4ee4f7-5b67-4b16-9025-d79d8158bba9/scratchpad/review-execution/exp1.py section (a): output row `long 101 ... entry_price 98.0 exit_price 98.0 initial_stop 99.0 risk_per_share 1.0 pnl 0.0 r_multiple 0.0 exit_reason stop bars_held 0`. Cause: `enter()` passes `sl=stop` validated by Backtesting only against the decision-minute close (backtesting.py new_order), and `_trade_table` line 296 uses `abs(entry - stop)` so the sign inversion is lost; line 303 then classifies any exit <= sl as 'stop'.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_trade_table`/`_open_trade_rows`, detect `side*(entry-stop) <= 0` and either tag these rows with a distinct exit_reason (e.g. 'stop_gapped_at_entry') or set risk_per_share/r_multiple to NaN and surface a count in metrics, so they are not pooled with genuine -1R stops. Document the behaviour in ENGINE_BEHAVIOR.md.

findings.title: ENGINE_BEHAVIOR claim 7 ('target gapped through fills at the better open') is false when the gap bar also touches the stop: resolved as a stop at the stop price, ignoring the known open
findings.failure_scenario: Long entered at 100 with stop 99 / target 101. The 09:42 minute opens at 103 (above the target), high 103.5, low 98.5 (below the stop), close 103. The first print of the minute (the open) is above the target, so a limit at 101 would fill at 103 as claim 7 states; instead Backtesting processes the SL order first (`orders.insert(0, ...)` for stop orders) and fills at min(open, stop)=99. Trade table: exit_price=99.0, exit_reason='stop', r_multiple=-1.0, when the only sequence consistent with the bar's open is a +3R target fill. The doc describes same-minute stop/target as 'unavoidable ambiguity', but here the open resolves the order of events and is ignored.
findings.evidence: Demonstrated with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dustin-Projects-strategy/bd4ee4f7-5b67-4b16-9025-d79d8158bba9/scratchpad/review-execution/exp1.py section (b): `long 99 ... entry 100.0 exit 99.0 initial_stop 99.0 target 101.0 pnl -99.0 r_multiple -1.0 exit_reason stop`. Library mechanics: backtesting.py lines ~888-932 (SL processed first; price = min(open, stop) for a sell stop). Only `test_target_gapped_through_fills_at_the_better_open` (no stop touch in the bar) backs claim 7; `test_stop_and_target_in_same_minute_resolves_to_stop` uses open=100 inside both levels, so neither test covers an open beyond the target. experiment.mark_ambiguous_exits would count this trade as ambiguous, so it is not silently lost, but the doc claim and the §'Unavoidable bar-resolution ambiguity' item 1 overstate what is unknowable.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend claim 7 and ambiguity item 1 to state that a same-minute stop touch takes precedence even when the bar OPENS beyond the target (pessimistic, not merely ambiguous), add a pinned test for that case, or special-case it in the engine (e.g. a market exit at the open when open is beyond the target) if the lab wants the open honoured.

findings.title: Comment in build_execution_frame says mid-data open positions are reported as `end_of_data`; the engine reports `open_at_end`, and the `end_of_data` branch in _trade_table is unreachable
findings.failure_scenario: Reader of build_execution_frame (line 116-118) expects an `end_of_data` exit_reason for the truncated last session; actual rows come from `_open_trade_rows` with exit_reason='open_at_end' (line 273), which is also the string metrics.py filters on. `_trade_table` line 308 can only produce 'end_of_data' for a closed trade that is neither in exit_reasons nor matches SL/TP, which cannot occur with finalize_trades=False and the lab's strategies; any future caller grepping for 'end_of_data' (e.g. to exclude open positions) would silently miss every open row.
findings.evidence: engine.py lines 116-118 vs 273; metrics.py line 67/69 and experiment.py line 159 filter on 'open_at_end' only; exp1.py section (c) shows the open row labelled 'open_at_end'. No test or code path emits 'end_of_data'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment at line 118 to `open_at_end`, and either remove the unreachable 'end_of_data' fallback in _trade_table or replace it with an explicit error/'unclassified' label so a genuinely unclassified closed trade is noticed rather than mislabelled.

verdicts.title: Stop gapped through at entry yields a zero-R 'stop' trade with a wrong-side initial_stop reported as positive risk
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by rerunning the reviewer's exp1.py section (a) at /home/dustin/Projects/strategy-lab (HEAD 80799e5): long with stop 99 decided at 09:40, 09:41 opens at 98 -> trade row `entry_price 98.0, exit_price 98.0, initial_stop 99.0, risk_per_share 1.0, pnl 0.0, r_multiple 0.0, exit_reason stop, bars_held 0`. Cause verified in src/stratlab/engine.py: `enter()` (line 174) passes `sl=stop` with no check against the eventual fill; `_trade_table` line 296 uses `abs(entry - stop)` so the inverted stop becomes a positive 1.0 risk, and line 303 classifies exit<=sl as 'stop'. metrics.trade_metrics (src/stratlab/metrics.py lines 67-93) then pools it into `trades`, `win_rate` (pnl<=0 counts as a loss when costs>0), `expectancy_r` (contributes 0) and `exit_reasons['stop']`. No flag anywhere distinguishes it from a genuine stop. Impact is bounded (R=0 rather than a falsely large loss, and only on gap-at-entry minutes), so minor stands.

verdicts.title: ENGINE_BEHAVIOR claim 7 ('target gapped through fills at the better open') is false when the gap bar also touches the stop: resolved as a stop at the stop price, ignoring the known open
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by rerunning exp1.py section (b): long entered 100, stop 99 / target 101, 09:42 bar O=103 H=103.5 L=98.5 C=103 -> `exit_price 99.0, exit_reason stop, r_multiple -1.0`. The bar's open (103) is the first known print and is above the target, yet the engine fills the stop at 99. docs/lab/ENGINE_BEHAVIOR.md line 16 states the target gap case fills at the better open without qualification, and the only backing test (`test_target_gapped_through_fills_at_the_better_open`, tests/test_engine_behavior.py:102-106) uses a bar whose low (102.5) never touches the stop; `test_stop_and_target_in_same_minute_resolves_to_stop` uses open=100 inside both levels. So no test covers open-beyond-target with a stop touch, and the doc's blanket claim and ambiguity item 1 ('path is unknown') overstate the case since the open resolves it. Mitigating: experiment.mark_ambiguous_exits (src/stratlab/experiment.py:121-139) would flag this row as ambiguous_exit (hi>=target and lo<=stop), so the trade is counted, not lost. Minor stands as a documentation/pessimism-labelling defect.

verdicts.title: Comment in build_execution_frame says mid-data open positions are reported as `end_of_data`; the engine reports `open_at_end`, and the `end_of_data` branch in _trade_table is unreachable
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by inspection and reproduction. src/stratlab/engine.py line 118 comment says 'reported as `end_of_data`'; the actual open-position rows come from `_open_trade_rows` with exit_reason='open_at_end' (line 273), reproduced in exp1.py section (c) (`open_at_end`, exit_time NaT). grep over src/, tests/, docs/ shows 'end_of_data' appears only at engine.py:118 (comment) and engine.py:308 (fallback in _trade_table); every consumer (metrics.py:67,69; experiment.py:159; template.html:225; test_engine_behavior.py:245; ENGINE_BEHAVIOR.md row 19) uses 'open_at_end'. With finalize_trades=False (line 224) and every discretionary exit recorded in exit_reasons via exit_all(), a closed trade that is neither in exit_reasons nor matches SL/TP cannot arise, so the line-308 label is dead and would mislabel any future unclassified trade rather than flag it. Minor: misleading comment plus dead/mislabelling fallback, no current wrong output.

findings.title: Freeze gate is a deny-list: only status == "PROPOSED" is refused, so an unlabelled or otherwise-labelled config runs on real data and writes LEDGER rows
findings.failure_scenario: Copy studies/vwap-ema9-2026-10/manifests/VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v0.1.toml and delete (or misspell, e.g. status = "DRAFT" or "PRE-REG") the `status = "PROPOSED"` line, then `stratlab run <file>` with no synthetic label: run_experiment() passes the gate, loads the real dataset, runs every variant, and appends rows to studies/vwap-ema9-2026-10/LEDGER.csv. The convention (docs/lab/HANDOFF.md step 1) is that only a FROZEN versioned file may run on real data; the code enforces the complement of one string rather than the required value.
findings.evidence: experiment.py:209-212: `if str(exp.get("status", "")).upper() == "PROPOSED" and not synthetic_label: raise PermissionError(...)`. A missing key yields "" which is != "PROPOSED" and runs. The committed demo config (experiments/demo_synthetic.toml) has no status field at all and relies on the synthetic label; a real-data config with the same omission is not stopped. test_proposed_config_refuses_real_data only covers the literal PROPOSED value.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert to an allow-list: `if not synthetic_label and str(exp.get("status", "")).upper() != "FROZEN": raise PermissionError(...)`, and add a test that a config with no status (and one with status = "DRAFT") is refused on real data.

findings.title: Ledger row is appended before the report is built; a report-build failure leaves a status=ok ledger row pointing at a run directory with no report.html
findings.failure_scenario: On a real-data run, `_append_ledger` writes one row per variant with status "ok", then `build_report` raises (e.g. `_vendor_assets` raises RuntimeError if the pinned itables bundle has an unexpected export clause, or any plotly/itables import error). run_experiment propagates the exception; the LEDGER.csv now has rows for a run whose directory holds run_record.json/metrics.json but no report.html, and because runs are immutable (FileExistsError on reuse of run_id) the row cannot be reconciled by re-running into the same id.
findings.evidence: experiment.py:279-283: `_append_ledger(...)` at line 280 precedes `from .report.build import build_report; build_report(run_dir, md=md, keep=keep)` at 282-283. Nothing catches a build_report failure or records it in the ledger/run_record.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the report (or at least import and vendor-check the report assets) before appending the ledger, or wrap build_report and record a `report_status` in run_record.json/ledger notes; alternatively write the ledger row last.

findings.title: Dataset SHA-256 verification is cached by (path, mtime, size): a same-size, same-mtime replacement passes verification on the second load in a process
findings.failure_scenario: Demonstrated in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dustin-Projects-strategy/bd4ee4f7-5b67-4b16-9025-d79d8158bba9/scratchpad/review-metrics/probe4.py: register a 1-row canonical file, resolve() once (SHA verified, close=1.5), overwrite the file with a same-length row (close=9.5) and restore mtime with os.utime; resolve() again returns success and read_canonical parses close=9.5 although the file's SHA no longer matches the registry. Within one long-lived process (CLI batch, notebook, test session) the module docstring's guarantee 'Every load verifies the SHA-256 before parsing' does not hold after the first load.
findings.evidence: store.py:67-69 `@lru_cache(maxsize=None) def _verified(path, mtime, size, expected)`; store.py:84 keys the lookup on `st.st_mtime, st.st_size`. Output of the probe: `size same: True | mtime same: True | file sha == registry: False` followed by `second resolve ACCEPTED tampered file; parsed close = 9.5`.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the cache (a 422k-row gz hashes in well under a second) or make load_dataset() hash the bytes it actually parses (hash the stream once and feed the same buffer to pandas), so verification and parse cannot diverge.

findings.title: `recent_Nm` window is never flagged partial, even when the available history is shorter than N months
findings.failure_scenario: coverage of 65 business sessions 2025-03-03..2025-05-30, warmup 5, recent_months=6 -> build_windows returns Window(id='recent_6m', label='Latest 6 months', start='2025-03-10', end='2025-05-30', sessions=60, partial=False). The window actually spans under 3 months and is identical to `full`, but the run record and report label it 'Latest 6 months' with partial=False, while the calendar halves in the same output are correctly flagged partial.
findings.evidence: windows.py:200-204 computes `rec = scored[scored >= start_bound]` and hard-codes `False` for `partial`; there is no check that `rec[0] <= start_bound` (i.e. that data existed at the start of the requested span). Reproduced in probe1.py (third block).
findings.suggested_fix: Set `partial = scored[0] > start_bound` (and append a note) so a clipped recent window is marked like the halves are.

findings.title: Concentration shares include losing trades in the top-k sum when there are fewer than k winners, understating dependence on big winners
findings.failure_scenario: pnl = [100, -50] -> concentration() returns top1_share_of_gross_profit=1.0 but top5_share_of_gross_profit=0.5 and top10_share=0.5. All gross profit comes from one trade, so every top-k share for k>=1 should be 1.0; the reported 0.5 arises because s.head(5) sums the -50 loser into 'top'. For a real strategy with, say, 8 winners and many losers, top10_share is pulled below top5_share and below 1.0, which reads as diversification that does not exist.
findings.evidence: metrics.py:105-107: `top = float(s.head(k).sum())` then `top / gross_profit` with no restriction to positive pnl. Reproduced in probe1.py (second block).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the share from positive trades only: `top_pos = float(s[s > 0].head(k).sum())` for the share, keeping `net - s.head(k).sum()` for net_pnl_ex_topk if 'remove the k largest trades' is the intended meaning (or restrict both and document).

findings.title: `avg_minutes_held` is reported in bars_held (exit_bar - entry_bar) while the report's 'mins' column and exposure_minutes_frac use bars_held + 1
findings.failure_scenario: A trade entered at minute i's open and stopped within minute i has bars_held=0. trade_metrics() reports avg_minutes_held=0.0 (probe1.py block 4), the report lists the same trade as mins=1 (build.py:141 `int(r.bars_held) + 1`), and experiment.py:160 counts it as 1 minute of exposure. metrics.json 'avg_minutes_held' is therefore systematically one minute lower than the trade-table minutes the reader sees, and the two cannot be reconciled from the report.
findings.evidence: metrics.py:87 `"avg_minutes_held": float(closed["bars_held"].mean())`; engine.py:319 `bars_held=int(r["ExitBar"] - r["EntryBar"])`; experiment.py:160 `(closed["bars_held"] + 1).sum() / len(frame)`; report/build.py:141 `"mins": int(r.bars_held) + 1`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `(closed["bars_held"] + 1).mean()` in trade_metrics (or rename the field to avg_bars_held) so the three places agree.

findings.title: Code identity hashes only *.py: report/template.html (which shapes report.html) is outside code_tree_sha256, and build_report can overwrite report.html inside an 'immutable' run directory
findings.failure_scenario: Edit src/stratlab/report/template.html (e.g. change how a statistic is labelled or which precomputed field a panel shows) with git stash-free dirty tree; code_identity() returns the same code_tree_sha256 (files_hashed=18, all .py), and `git status --porcelain -- src` does flag it only if the file is tracked and modified. Then `stratlab report <run_dir>` regenerates report.html in an existing run directory with the new template, while run_record.json still carries the original identity. Two reports produced from the same run_record with different templates are indistinguishable by the recorded identity.
findings.evidence: experiment.py:60 `files = sorted(p for p in src.rglob("*.py"))`; `git ls-files src | grep -v .py` shows src/stratlab/report/template.html is a tracked non-.py source; report/build.py:187-188 `out = run_dir / "report.html"; out.write_text(html)` with no existence check, unlike run_experiment's FileExistsError guard at experiment.py:225-226.
findings.suggested_fix: Hash `rglob("*")` for regular files under src/stratlab (or explicitly add template.html), and have build_report refuse to overwrite an existing report.html unless an explicit rebuild flag is passed, recording the rebuild (template hash + time) in a sidecar rather than silently replacing the file.

verdicts.title: Freeze gate is a deny-list: only status == "PROPOSED" is refused, so an unlabelled or otherwise-labelled config runs on real data and writes LEDGER rows
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by code: src/stratlab/experiment.py:209 `if str(exp.get("status", "")).upper() == "PROPOSED" and not synthetic_label: raise PermissionError`. A missing key yields "" and any other value (DRAFT, PRE-REG, a typo of PROPOSED) also compares unequal, so the gate falls through to prepare_market + run + _append_ledger (line 280, guarded only by `ledger and not synthetic_label`). The committed demo config experiments/demo_synthetic.toml has no status key and the only test (tests/test_experiment_pipeline.py:107) covers the literal PROPOSED value. docs/lab/HANDOFF.md:35-36 states the convention that a FROZEN file is what gets run; the code enforces the complement of one string, i.e. fails open. Not reproduced on real data (would violate the blind-experiment constraint), but the logic is unconditional. Kept at major: a pre-registration gate that fails open on a misspelling or omitted key is a governance control defect, not a style issue.

verdicts.title: Ledger row is appended before the report is built; a report-build failure leaves a status=ok ledger row pointing at a run directory with no report.html
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by code order: experiment.py:279-283 writes run_record.json, metrics.json, then `_append_ledger(...)` at 280, then `from .report.build import build_report; build_report(run_dir, md=md, keep=keep)` at 282-283 with no try/except. report/build.py `_vendor_assets` (lines 29-45) has two `raise RuntimeError` paths and imports itables/plotly at call time, so a build failure after the ledger write is a real path. Run dirs are immutable (FileExistsError at experiment.py:225-226), so the orphaned ledger row cannot be reconciled by re-running into the same id. Not demonstrated end-to-end because doing so would require writing LEDGER.csv inside the repository, which is forbidden for this reviewer; the static ordering is unambiguous. Minor is the right severity: results are not wrong, the ledger just points at a run without its HTML.

verdicts.title: Dataset SHA-256 verification is cached by (path, mtime, size): a same-size, same-mtime replacement passes verification on the second load in a process
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dustin-Projects-strategy/bd4ee4f7-5b67-4b16-9025-d79d8158bba9/scratchpad/review-verify-metrics/probe.py: registered a 1-row canonical file (close=1.5), resolve() verified it, overwrote with a same-length row (close=9.5) and restored mtime via os.utime; output `same mtime/size True True sha matches False` then `second resolve ACCEPTED; parsed {... 'Close': 9.5 ...}`. Cause is store.py:67-69 `@lru_cache(maxsize=None) def _verified(path, mtime, size, expected)` keyed at store.py:84 on `st.st_mtime, st.st_size`. The module docstring (store.py:1-6) claims 'Every load verifies the SHA-256 before parsing', which does not hold after the first load within a process. Requires an in-process same-size, mtime-preserving replacement, so minor.

verdicts.title: `recent_Nm` window is never flagged partial, even when the available history is shorter than N months
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: coverage of 65 business sessions 2025-03-03..2025-05-30 (present==minutes), warmup 5, recent_months=6 -> build_windows returns `Window(id='recent_6m', label='Latest 6 months', start='2025-03-10', end='2025-05-30', sessions=60, kind='recent', partial=False, ...)` while the 2025H1 half in the same output is correctly `partial=True, note='clipped to available data'`. windows.py:58-63 computes `rec = scored[scored >= start_bound]` and hard-codes `False` for partial with no check that scored[0] <= start_bound. The window is identical to `full` but labelled as a 6-month window with partial=False. Mislabelling only, affects report/run-record metadata, so minor.

verdicts.title: Concentration shares include losing trades in the top-k sum when there are fewer than k winners, understating dependence on big winners
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: `concentration(pd.Series([100.0, -50.0]))` returns `top1_share_of_gross_profit: 1.0, top5_share_of_gross_profit: 0.5, top10_share_of_gross_profit: 0.5`. metrics.py:105-107 sums `s.head(k)` without restricting to positive pnl, so once k exceeds the number of winners the share is pulled below 1.0 (and below smaller-k shares), reading as diversification that does not exist. The `net_pnl_ex_topk` field is arguably correct under a 'remove the k largest trades' reading, but the share-of-gross-profit metric is wrong for k > number of winners. Minor: a secondary diagnostic metric, not a headline statistic, and only wrong when winners < k.

verdicts.title: `avg_minutes_held` is reported in bars_held (exit_bar - entry_bar) while the report's 'mins' column and exposure_minutes_frac use bars_held + 1
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by code: metrics.py:87 `"avg_minutes_held": float(closed["bars_held"].mean())`; engine.py:319 `bars_held=int(r["ExitBar"] - r["EntryBar"])`; experiment.py:160 `(closed["bars_held"] + 1).sum() / len(frame)`; report/build.py:141 `"mins": int(r.bars_held) + 1`; template.html:221 displays the metric as 'Avg minutes held'. bars_held=0 is a real, tested outcome (tests/test_engine_behavior.py:77 asserts `t.bars_held == 0` for a stop hit in the entry minute; ENGINE_BEHAVIOR.md row 4). So the headline 'Avg minutes held' is systematically one minute below the per-trade 'mins' column and the exposure calculation. Minor: an off-by-one labelling inconsistency, not a wrong P&L.

verdicts.title: Code identity hashes only *.py: report/template.html (which shapes report.html) is outside code_tree_sha256, and build_report can overwrite report.html inside an 'immutable' run directory
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by code: experiment.py:60 `files = sorted(p for p in src.rglob("*.py"))`; `git ls-files src | grep -v .py` returns exactly src/stratlab/report/template.html; report/build.py:187-188 `out = run_dir / "report.html"; out.write_text(html)` has no existence guard, and cli.py:49-51 exposes `stratlab report <run_dir>` which calls it on an existing run dir. Partial mitigation the finding already acknowledges: git_commit and `git status --porcelain -- src` (experiment.py:70) do capture a committed or tracked-and-modified template change, so the identity is not blind to it, only code_tree_sha256 is. The overwrite of report.html in an otherwise immutable run directory is real. Minor: identity is still recoverable from git_commit/git_dirty_paths; this is a gap in the content hash and the immutability guard, not a wrong result.

findings.title: Drawdown panel recomputed in JS disagrees with 'Max DD (session close)' metric (peak not seeded with starting cash)
findings.failure_scenario: renderEquity() computes dd with `let peak = -Infinity; ... e/peak - 1`, so the first session's equity defines the peak and any loss on day 1 (or any run that never exceeds starting capital before a new low) shows as 0% / too-shallow drawdown. metrics.equity_metrics prepends initial_cash before cummax. Demonstrated on the demo run: VWR3 first-session equity 99,542.41 -> JS panel minimum -9.04% while the metrics table shows Max DD (session close) -9.43% for the same window. For a window where equity falls from the start and never recovers to $100k the panel would read ~0% at the start of the drawdown while the metric correctly shows the loss from $100k.
findings.evidence: Scripted check in headless Chrome on the demo report: `dd VWR3 :: {js_min:-0.09037, metric:-0.09435, first_eq:99542.41}`; all other variants whose first session closed above 100,000 match exactly. metrics.py lines 41-43 (`eq_with_start = pd.concat([pd.Series([initial_cash]), ...])`).
findings.suggested_fix: Seed the peak with the window's starting cash: `let peak = R.execution.cash;` (fresh-capital windows all start at execution.cash per the eqNote text). Alternatively embed the Python drawdown series so the panel is a pure view.

findings.title: Trade table 'Min' column uses bars_held+1 while 'Avg minutes held' metric uses bars_held — same quantity shown with two conventions
findings.failure_scenario: build.py embeds `mins = bars_held + 1` per trade (so a trade entered 12:05 and exited 12:06 shows 'Min 2', entry 09:45/exit 11:20 shows 96), but metrics.trade_metrics reports avg_minutes_held = mean(bars_held). The displayed per-trade minutes therefore average exactly 1.0 more than the 'Avg minutes held' row of the metrics table; a reader reconciling the table against the metric gets a contradiction. Exposure (experiment.py:160) uses bars_held+1, so the three displayed quantities use two definitions.
findings.evidence: Headless check on demo: `VWR0 mean table Min :: 27.0997`, `metric avg_minutes_held :: 26.0997`. metrics.py:87 `"avg_minutes_held": float(closed["bars_held"].mean())`; experiment.py:160 `(closed["bars_held"] + 1)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one definition of minutes held and use it in build.py:141, metrics.py:87 and experiment.py:160 (or label the column 'Bars spanned'); document whether the entry minute counts.

findings.title: Experiment title inserted into <title> without HTML escaping — config string can break the document head / inject script
findings.failure_scenario: `tpl.replace("__TITLE__", ... + title)` uses the raw `experiment.title` from the TOML/run record. A title containing `</title><script>...</script>` or just `&`/`<` is emitted verbatim into <head>. Every other config string (labels, hypothesis, synthetic banner) goes through esc() in JS; this is the one unescaped sink and the only server-side one.
findings.evidence: Rebuilt a scratch copy with title `Demo & x` via `stratlab report`; output contains `SYNTHETIC · Demo & x` and the browser title is truncated to 'SYNTHETIC · Demo '. Variant label `` was correctly escaped in the DOM (only appears inside the JSON payload).
findings.suggested_fix: `import html` and use `html.escape(title)` for the __TITLE__ substitution (and consider escaping ids used in `data-w`/`data-v` attributes in template.html:260/262).

findings.title: Report size will be ~15-16 MB on the real corpus (~490 sessions), at or over the 16 MB artifact limit
findings.failure_scenario: Demo report (181 scored sessions, 6 variants, 2 feature sets, 5,112 trades) is 9.29 MB: 5.58 MB vendored Plotly+DataTables + 3.72 MB JSON payload, of which bars = 1.95 MB (two feature sets x 181 days x 7 arrays), trades = 1.40 MB, results = 0.28 MB (diff_vs_baseline.keys lists are embedded but never rendered). Scaling the payload linearly to ~490 sessions gives ~10.1 MB payload + 5.58 MB vendor ≈ 15.6 MB — within noise of the 16 MB artifact cap, and any variant with more trades per session or a third feature set (different minutes/ema/vwap_source) pushes it over.
findings.evidence: Measured from the generated demo: total 9,293,478 bytes; `data bytes 3717145`; `bars 1951818` (fsets '5m|hlc3|9','3m|ohlc4|9', 181 days each); per-variant trades 116-403 KB; VWR2 results 100,984 bytes of which diff_vs_baseline 40,238 bytes (keys lists). Chrome DOM dump of the rendered page is 9.6 MB.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip `diff_vs_baseline.keys` and `library_stats` from the embedded results; round vwap/ema to 2 dp and emit bar arrays as compact numeric arrays (or gzip+base64 the payload and inflate with DecompressionStream); consider embedding 1 feature set per distinct `minutes` only, or dropping non-trade days from bars.

findings.title: `stratlab report` rebuild renders 'Signals use completed -minute bars' when no bar data is embedded

findings.title: Zero/near-zero deltas get a '+' sign and green colour for lower-is-better metrics

findings.title: Pre-registration gates disagree between the proposal (md) and the experiment TOML; VWR4's md gate is unmeasurable
findings.failure_scenario: Both files are to be frozen as v1.0 and then interpreted against. VWR4 md row (line 45) says evidence is uninformative if '...VWR0's morning subset (from the diff) is statistically indistinguishable from its afternoon subset' — no test, no threshold, and the diff table does not split VWR0 by time of day; the TOML (VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v0.1.toml:92) drops that clause entirely ('Fewer than 100 morning trades.'). Conversely VWR0's own uninformative-if (TOML:48, '<200 trades in the full window, or sign change when top 5 removed') appears nowhere in the md. After the run, a reader choosing which frozen document governs can flip whether VWR4 or VWR0 counts as informative.
findings.evidence: VWR_FAMILY_PROPOSAL_v0.1.md:40-45 vs VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v0.1.toml:38-48 and :83-92. The md gives no uninformative-if for VWR0 at all (section 'VWR0 — baseline', lines 27-36). IGP0 TOML:104 'uninformative_if' is a disclaimer ('Always partly uninformative...'), not a criterion either.
findings.suggested_fix: Before freezing v1.0, make the TOML the single machine-readable source of hypothesis/metric/uninformative-if and have the md reference it (or generate the md table from the TOML). Replace the VWR4 subset clause with a concrete, computable test (e.g. Welch t on R of VWR0 trades entered <=11:30 vs >11:30, |t|<1) or drop it; add VWR0's gate to the md; give IGP0 a real criterion (trade count / top-5 sign flip).

findings.title: Frozen manifest does not pin code identity; the §c claim in scripts/README.md is not what the mechanism delivers
findings.failure_scenario: VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v1.0.toml (frozen) will reference 'stratlab.strategies.vwap_reclaim:VwapReclaim' with no version or hash. After the freeze, edit src/stratlab/strategies/common.py line 27 (e.g. make vwap_prev cross-session) or indicators.py/engine.py/sessions.py — none of which the 'new class or module' rule covers — and run the unchanged frozen TOML: the run succeeds, results differ, and the only trace is a different code_tree_sha256 in run_record/ledger that nothing pre-registered can be checked against. run_experiment also does not refuse a dirty src tree (experiment.py:71-72 records git_dirty_paths only), and the real-data gate at experiment.py:209 blocks only status == 'PROPOSED', so a TOML with status 'DRAFT', 'frozen?' or no status runs on real data.
findings.evidence: scripts/README.md:8-10 claims §c is satisfied by 'a NEW strategy class or module... the old one stays' plus recording git commit/tree SHA. docs/conventions.md §c (lines 45-49) requires retired versions kept alongside; the §-preamble allows an override only 'explicitly and deliberately... in writing, with a reason' — the README presents compliance, not an override. VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v0.1.toml has no code hash field; experiment.py:57-73, 205-212.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `code_commit` and `code_tree_sha256` (and `backtesting` version) to the frozen v1.0 TOML and make run_experiment refuse on mismatch or when src is dirty; gate real-data runs on status == 'FROZEN' rather than != 'PROPOSED'. Either state in scripts/README.md that this is a written §c override (git-addressed versioning instead of retained script copies) with the reason, or keep per-run snapshots of src/stratlab/strategies in the run dir.

findings.title: IG-P0 code suppresses the EMA/VWAP cross on a session's first 3m bar; the rule table presents the bare formula and a 09:33 window start
findings.failure_scenario: Synthetic demo: day 1 flat at 100 (EMA == VWAP at the close), day 2 flat at 99. On day 2's first completed 3m bar EMA=99.80 > VWAP=99.00 and the previous bar had EMA<=VWAP, so the table's formula (ema[t-1] <= vwap[t-1] and ema[t] > vwap[t]) — and TradingView's ta.crossover, which uses the prior bar regardless of session — fires at 09:30-09:33. The lab code produces 0 trades because common.py sets ema_prev/vwap_prev to NaN on each session's first bar (groupby(session).shift(1)) and instagram_austin_vwap_ema9.py:62 returns on NaN. The creator's own short example (frame t=47 s, Mo 28 Sep) is an opening-drop situation where EMA sits far above the freshly reset VWAP. The table's 'Decisions on bars ending 09:33' is therefore never true; the earliest possible entry is the bar ending 09:36.
findings.evidence: src/stratlab/strategies/common.py:16-18, 27-28; src/stratlab/strategies/instagram_austin_vwap_ema9.py:62, 68; SOURCE_RULES_IG_AUSTIN_v0.1.md rows 'Entry event' (line 37) and 'Time window' (line 46) make no mention of the exclusion. Demo script output: rule-table formula fires at ['09:30']; lab code fires at []; trades: 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rule-table row 'Cross on the session's first bar (EMA vs reset VWAP)': Source — / Kind — / Lab assumption: excluded (or included) — and make it a reviewer decision, since TradingView would show it as a cross. Correct the window text to the effective 09:36 start if exclusion stays. Same disclosure applies to VWR2 (trigger 'ema_vwap_cross'), though its 09:45 start makes it moot in practice.

findings.title: Trials accounting omits the pre-committed raw-corpus rerun and the TOML lacks dsr_threshold_implied required by §b amendment
findings.failure_scenario: The proposal (line 83) and HANDOFF item 3 commit, before the first run, to 'rerun VWR0 on the raw corpus and report the difference'. That is a seventh configuration evaluated on this corpus, with its own ledger row, but trials_planned = 6; the implied hurdle is 0.934 at N=6 vs 0.997 at N=7 (metrics.expected_max_sharpe(7, 489)). The rerun also has no TOML yet, so when it is written its own trials_planned and status will be chosen after the main result is known. Separately, docs/conventions.md §b amendment 2026-07-30 says every run manifest records both trials_planned AND dsr_threshold_implied; the TOML records only trials_planned (the 0.93 figure lives only in the md, line 25).
findings.evidence: VWR0_EXPERIMENT_v0.1.toml:15-21 (no dsr field); VWR_FAMILY_PROPOSAL_v0.1.md:25, :83; docs/lab/HANDOFF.md:23, :38-39; docs/conventions.md:37-42; experiment.py:231 computes the hurdle from exp.trials_planned per config file.
findings.suggested_fix: Either count the raw rerun (trials_planned = 7, hurdle ~1.00) or state in the manifest why a same-rules/different-data-view rerun is excluded from N. Add `dsr_threshold_implied = "0.934 ann. (N=6, T=489)"` to the TOML. Write the raw-corpus rerun's TOML (mask = none, status FROZEN alongside v1.0) now, so it is pre-registered too.

findings.title: Mask v1.0 makes 9 five-minute and 8 three-minute signal bars incomplete; strategies still trade on them and the proposal says signals use completed bars
